title: MSDR: Multi-Step Dependency Relation Networks for Spatial Temporal Forecasting

problem.claim: Spatial temporal forecasting in traffic networks must handle complicated and long-range spatial-temporal dependencies.

gap.claim: The authors argue that implicit representations learned by temporal extracting modules are insufficient for capturing long-range spatial dependencies.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Multi-Step Dependency Relation (MSDR), a recurrent neural network variant that uses hidden states from multiple historical time steps at each time unit.
The paper develops two strategies for incorporating spatial information into dependency-relation embeddings between multiple historical time steps and the current time step.
The paper proposes the Graph-based MSDR (GMSDR) framework, which integrates graph-based neural networks with MSDR for general spatial-temporal forecasting applications.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating the proposed approach on several popular datasets.
The authors report that GMSDR outperforms state-of-the-art methods by an obvious margin.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatial temporal forecasting is important for intelligent transportation systems.
Traffic-network forecasting is difficult because of complicated and long-range spatial-temporal dependencies.
Existing deep-learning approaches learn spatial and temporal representations, but the authors argue that temporal-module representations do not sufficiently capture long-range spatial dependencies.
MSDR uses multiple historical hidden states and adds strategies for spatial information in dependency-relation embeddings; GMSDR integrates MSDR with graph-based neural networks.
The approach is evaluated on several datasets, with the authors reporting an obvious-margin improvement over state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The proposed recurrent architecture explicitly uses multiple historical time-step representations rather than only the latest hidden state.

interpretation.claim: Explicit multi-step dependency modeling may help address long-range dependencies that are not adequately captured by a single latest hidden state.

application.claim: For forecasting tasks with long-range temporal and spatial dependencies, consider architectures that expose multiple historical states to each update unit.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which datasets, metrics, or conditions determine the reported advantage.

unknowns: Details of the two spatial-information strategies
